title: Averages of the complement indicator vanish at a density-one point
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and b ∈ ℝ^n. Suppose λ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(b))/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺, with the quotient taken in [0, ∞]. Then ⨍_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ → 0 as s → 0⁺. Here λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, and the averages are Bochner set averages of the real-valued indicator function of the complement of B.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (b : Euclid n), MeasurableSet B → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => volume (B ∩ closedBall b ρ) / volume (closedBall b ρ)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ⨍ a in closedBall b s, Bᶜ.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) a ∂volume) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
